title: First-person tower defense I built in a few days just by prompting AI
author: ElusiveSim
selftext:
Browser game, built entirely by prompting an AI agent I made called Elusive.  
  
Fight off waves of increasingly large enemies, get money, and buy turrets.  
  
To play it or build your own game, google "elusive sim".

comments.author: SmoggySPECTEREGaming
comments.body: What did you prompt to create the scalable building with staircases, or did you build that by hand in blender?

replies.author: EverythingBOffensive
replies.body: I've had gpt convert and import 3d models from the internet before so anything is possible!

replies.author: ElusiveSim
replies.body:
Buildings are already in Elusive's template so all users can get customized buildings just by asking for them. The buildings and all models except the characters are generated at runtime.  
  
When I first created them, I prompted incrementally. First I prompted for one room, then a room with walls with a door, then with a door and windows, then multiple stories with staircases. Each of those steps required some corrective prompts too.

comments.author: InitialCreature
comments.body: how do you handle your stairs so smoothly? I use a blend of invisible ramp plane for collision and a ramp spring hoverboard controller but it never feels smooth.

replies.author: ElusiveSim
replies.body: I use Rapier physics engine's (Javascript version) [character controller](https://rapier.rs/docs/user_guides/javascript/character_controller). But Rapier has some bugs and if I had more time I'd try switching to Jolt which also [handles stairs well](https://jrouwe.github.io/JoltPhysics.js/character_virtual.html).

replies.author: InitialCreature
replies.body: yeah I'm using a hybrid on rapier with custom stuff. Rapier has a bug with friction causing players to lock to floors and walls, so I had to turn it off completely and write a custom friction solution.

replies.author: ElusiveSim
replies.body: My NPCs don't use the Rapier character controller because it's too slow for many entities and they are physics-based (like yours I think). They use a controller modeled after [https://github.com/pmndrs/ecctrl](https://github.com/pmndrs/ecctrl). So using that as a reference is another option if you want to stick with Rapier. But I would recommend trying Jolt if you're willing to switch engines.

replies.author: InitialCreature
replies.body: unfortunately at this point it's too late to switch to anything else, 5 months on the stack at this point but I've been able to work around its quirks
